text:
Anya: Quick q—how should gateway rank an exact-host + prefix vs wildcard-host + header-anchor? Example:

Anya: Route A:
```
host: api.redwood.ai
path: /api/v1/users/*
service: users-v1
```
Anya: Route B:
```
host: *.redwood.ai
path: /api/*
headers:
  x-service: users
service: users-legacy
```
Anya: If request to api.redwood.ai/api/v1/users with x-service=users which wins? We're seeing weird flip-flop when traffic hits edge.

Miguel: I think concrete host should beat wildcard hosts. Host specificity first, then path specificity, then header anchors.
Miguel: But header anchors are > path segments in some current impl, which causes B to win when x-service present.

Sam: Problem is current score ties when path lengths similar; header presence adds points but we didn't normalize by host specificity.
Sam: Proposal: scoring vector [host_specificity, path_specificity, anchor_matches, rule_age]. Compare lexicographically.

Elena: Lexicographic vector seems good. Add deterministic tie-breaker: rule ID or creation_ts.
Elena: Also surface the vector in Console match trace so owners can debug.

Anya: Nice. For path_specificity use number of static segments, penalize wildcards. Eg /api/v1/users -> 3 static, /api/* -> 1 static.

Sam: Also normalize headers by weight type: exact header match = full point, regex capture = 0.7, presence=0.3.

Miguel: One more: route rollouts need to let us force header-anchored precedence for internal egress (eg: canary routing). Add explicit priority flag "anchor_priority: true" to override scoring.

Anya: Can we make default scoring backwards compatible? If not present, use existing behavior for 6 months then flip.

Elena: +1 on opt-in flag. We should add lint rule to warn when two rules could tie; deploy-bot could annotate.

deploy-bot: lint-check: route collision potential detected between routes users-v1 and users-legacy. See: https://console.redwood.ai/rules/2198765432

Sam: I'll open RFC PR with example matrix and console trace mockups. Will include benchmark of scoring on our 10k route dataset.

Anya: Thanks — ok if we land RFC early next week? Need this for dedicated rollout tests.

Miguel: fine by me. I'll prototype comparator in go and send to sam.

Elena: I'll add Console trace mockups to the PR.

Anya: :thumbsup:
